title: SLO-aware request lifecycles and cross-SDK idempotency semantics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Context: We're seeing inconsistent client-side behavior across languages when services approach SLO boundaries (p95/p99 latency and error budgets). SDKs currently implement ad-hoc timeouts, retry counts, and hedging semantics which produces duplicate work, unclear billing exposure, and operational noise in multi-region failover scenarios. This ticket defines a cross-SDK standard for SLO-aware request lifecycles, idempotency key semantics, hedged requests, and sensible circuit-breaker defaults tied to service error budgets and region health.
decision_summary: Adopt an SLO-driven client timeout budget: each route publishes a server-side budget (recommended: target_tail_ms and p99_guard_ms). SDKs compute per-request budget = min(client_max_budget, route_target_tail_ms * safety_factor). Hedging allowed only when request is safe to retry (idempotent) or when client provides Idempotency-Key header. Default hedged fanout=2, hedge_delay = 0.6 * per-request-budget. Circuit-breaker thresholds will be derived from the service error budget window (open when error_rate > threshold OR sustained p99 > p99_guard). Load-shedding is done at the earliest deterministic layer (edge) using dynamic token buckets and priority hints from the client (e.g., X-Request-Priority).
proposed_api_and_contracts: 1) Idempotency: introduce a canonical header 'Idempotency-Key' (UUID v4 recommended). Servers must persist idempotency outcomes for the route's idempotency_ttl (default 24h). SDKs should surface helper: generateIdempotencyKey() and auto-attach for calls marked 'non-destructive'. 2) Hedging API: SDK option 'hedging.enabled' (false by default), 'hedging.max_attempts' (default 2), 'hedging.hedge_delay_ms' (computed but overrideable). 3) Timeout/Deadline API: per-call 'deadline_ms' and optional 'slo_hint' string to match route published SLO. 4) Circuit breaker: SDK-level circuit breaker config accepts thresholds but can subscribe to server-side 'breaker_advice' header to converge behavior across clients.
implementation_notes: - Step 1: Define route metadata schema (target_tail_ms, p99_guard_ms, idempotency_support, idempotency_ttl) and add to model catalog + API gateway. - Step 2: Add server-side idempotency store (sharded, TTL-backed). - Step 3: Implement client SDK helpers (python/js/go) with unified low-level transport layer for hedging and deadline calculation. - Step 4: Add observability: 'duplicate_request_rate', 'idempotency_cache_hit_ratio', 'hedged_success_first_attempt_pct', and cost delta metrics. - Step 5: Run canary in us-west-2 on ~1% traffic targeting read-heavy routes and a controlled write route with idempotency injection.
rollout_plan: A: Spec and server-side proto changes merged (PR: platform/api#1832). B: Implement and ship SDK helpers behind a feature-flag (python/js/go). C: Canary hedging on low-cost read endpoints (2 weeks). D: Enable for broader routes with automated monitoring and automatic rollback triggers if duplicate_request_rate > 0.1% or cost_per_token increases > 5% without latency gains. E: Post-mortem and adjustments before GA.
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency key storage/lookup, integration tests that validate single-response semantics under simulated retries and hedged responses, chaos tests that inject cross-region latency and partial failures, and load tests to measure idempotency store latency and memory pressure. Add experiment to measure p99 tail improvement vs cost delta.
monitoring_and_slo_checks: Track per-route: success_rate, client_errors, server_errors, p50/p95/p99 latency, idempotency_duplicate_rate, hedged_request_fraction, and cost_per_1000_tokens. Add alert when: (1) idempotency_duplicate_rate increases by +X from baseline, (2) p99 latency regresses for >15m, (3) error budget burn rate > 2x. Create Grafana dashboard and pager runbook linked below.
runbook_actions: If hedging causes unsafe duplicates: disable hedging flag, mark affected routes as 'no_hedge', increase idempotency ttl to avoid late duplicates, roll back SDK change. If circuit breaker opens frequently: investigate root cause (region outage vs client misconfig), lower hedging rate, or increase retry backoff windows. Document emergency steps in /runbooks/retries-and-hedging.md.
